I am an old woman now, sixty-one years, and I have worked this small barley plot for many seasons. My plot is small, only about a third of a hectare, so one bag of DAP from the cooperative is enough if I can get it — I will try for one bag and add a little urea at tillering if cash allows, but I do not push much nitrogen on barley because too much makes it fall over before harvest. I save my own barley seed from last year like my mother did; the improved seed is not easy to find for barley here, and I trust what grew well on my plot. I put the manure from my few animals on this plot because it is my own land and I want the soil to stay strong, and I work it mostly myself with help from my daughter, only hiring a few days for ploughing since I am too old to follow the oxen.
